sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r5/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: 'Quality Checks'!A2:E2 (row 1, instruction_is_a_natural_product_request) and 'Internal Quality Checks'!A2:E2 (same text, annotation column E empty)
evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md is a first-person request from a small firm: it opens with the business problem ('our clients keep emailing documents to whoever answered last. We want a secure chat where each client talks to us inside their legal matter'), names the two priorities in prose with motivation ('Two things matter more than anything else. First, ethical walls... Second, retention'), and closes with a user-style acceptance request ('please try it the way we'll use it, in a browser... We only ever use it through the pages'). It contains none of the quality-checks.md:11 defect markers: no numbered acceptance list, no shall/must spec table, no feature matrix, no framework choice, no endpoint list. Its only file-layout mentions (/assets/seed_data.json, /instructions, /app/server.js, /app/app.db) are the runtime contract that row 4 requires to be stated, given in one sentence. The referenced notes keep the same voice and justify rules from practice ('a leak is a professional-conduct problem for us', 'Our internet in court is patchy', 'People fix typos and figures'). The one table (walls-and-retention.md:5-11) lists seed accounts, not requirements, and integration.md's runtime facts (Node 22, 0.0.0.0:3000, NODE_PATH, DB_PATH, GET /api/health) are template-mandated operating details written as 'how we run it' prose rather than a build recipe; no framework, page structure or API routes for features are dictated. Residual observation (not a defect): the notes are requirement-dense (for example conversations.md 'at least three levels deep', '390 px wide'), but each is a concrete user-facing expectation in conversational prose, not a checklist. This row grades prompt style only, so broken-app/conforming-alternative probes do not bear on it; no runtime evidence is required.
